_doc: Point-in-time fact sheet for CHTR (Charter Communications, Inc., CIK 1091667), generated by retro/generators/chtr/gen_chtr.py from the filings; every value is tied to a source and becomes visible only on or after its 'published' date (EDGAR's acceptance time in ET: accepted at or after 16:00, the next trading day). It holds what decides whether a date can be built under method r2, and nothing else: each 10-K vintage's Item 6 EPS history, the listing record and the price basis. Every period of 1999-2013 is a loss per share except the Predecessor's eleven months to 2009-11-30 (the Plan and fresh start gains) and the Successor's first month (December 2009), neither of them a year, so no date of 2008-2013 has a full year of positive EPS to anchor a P/E and none is built (retro/README.md, "CHTR 2008-2009"). No print, guide, dividend, signal or theme event is transcribed (no dividend was paid: 'no_dividend' quotes the 10-Ks), and the builder refuses any date that passes the gate until they are. Extended with 2014-2017 by retro/generators/chtr/gen_chtr_1417.py: the FY2014-FY2016 10-K vintages, the Q4 2014-2016 releases' full years ('q4_actuals'), the one-off test of FY2016 (the only positive year to 2016: $15.94 diluted with the approximately $3.3 billion valuation allowance reversal, excluded by the mirror of the AAPL FY2002 test), the listing and the Parent Merger's exchange ratio; still no print, guide, signal or rule-T value, as no date of 2014-2017 passes the gate (retro/README.md, "CHTR 2014-2017").
price_basis: Yahoo's CHTR series is the Successor's Class A common stock from its first point, 2010-01-05 (firstTradeDate; the stock quoted on the OTC Bulletin Board as CCMM from December 2009 and listed on NASDAQ as CHTR from 2010-09-14). Yahoo serves no close of the Predecessor's Class A common stock (NASDAQ: CHTR to 2009-04-06, then the OTC Bulletin Board or the Pink Sheets to its cancellation on 2009-11-30) under CHTR or any other symbol read (CHTRQ, CCMM: not found).

2016.item: the reversal of approximately $3.3 billion of Legacy Charter's valuation allowance on its deferred tax assets, recognized as an income tax benefit
2016.quote_nonrecurring: absent non-recurring impacts such as the reversal of the income tax valuation allowance in the second quarter of 2016, we may incur net losses in the future.
2016.quote_amount: As a result, Charter has reversed approximately $3.3 billion of its valuation allowance and recognized a corresponding income tax benefit in the consolidated statements of operations for the year ended December 31, 2016.
2016.note: net income attributable to Charter shareholders $3,522M (income before income taxes $820M, income tax benefit $2,925M, noncontrolling interests $223M); without the $3,300M valuation allowance reversal $222M, so the listed benefit exceeds the year's income without it and reported EPS is more than double the EPS without it (the mirror of the AAPL FY2002 test); no filing publishes a figure excluding only it

net_of_listed_charges.note: the reversal plus the other pension benefits ($899M) less the merger and restructuring costs ($900M) and the loss on extinguishment of debt ($111M), the pre-tax items taken whole, the CB FY2005 netting
